Variants.Content: Brymond City is located deep in the Red Mountains in the west of Dorne. It is the traditional castle of the Brymond family. This is the world of the Stoney Dornish people: rocky slopes, narrow valleys, thin water sources and winding mountain passes are more important than harbors and rivers. Castles can monitor mountain roads, but they cannot fertilize barren hills; locals rely on herds, springs, mountain fields, and familiarity with the roads. The Red Mountains serve as both a barrier to Dorne and a dangerous frontier to the Reach and the Westerlands. The fixed significance of Blymont lies in the mountain society, border defense and regional differences within Dorne, not in who is holding what flag at a certain moment.

Entry Blackmont Castle A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Blackmont Castle They care about wells and springs, irrigation canals, orchards, drought-tolerant livestock, and routes to avoid the scorching sun. They also look at whether seeds are left after collecting grain and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
